book.universe.probe_log.page.1:
UNV-7 SURVEY PROBE LOG

Main engine failure. Forced landing on this planet. Hull breached, primary systems offline.

To whoever finds this: the gear aboard can still be repaired.
book.universe.probe_log.page.2:
[MULTITOOL]
Damaged in the impact. Two copper ingots, two redstone and an iron ingot will fix it.

Hold USE: mining laser. It overheats if fired too long.
Sneak + USE: scan for nearby ore veins.
book.universe.probe_log.page.3:
[EXOSUIT]
Helmet and chestplate seal in your oxygen; the full set holds off cold, heat, toxins and radiation.

Oxygen capsules: bottled leaves.
Hazard cells: copper, redstone, coal.

Jetpack: jump again in mid-air.
book.universe.probe_log.page.4:
[SHIPS]
Build one from blocks: a helm, thrusters, fuel tanks; dress the hull as you like. Use the helm to assemble.

Fill the tanks with launch fuel (coal, gunpowder, a glass bottle).
Climb past the sky to reach space.
book.universe.probe_log.page.5:
[COURSE]
This planet has a moon: airless and cold, but rich in titanium.

In space the impulse engine gets you there fast. Fly into a body's atmosphere to land.

Better equipment needs titanium.
book.universe.probe_log.page.6:
[MISSION]
This probe belongs to the Universe Survey Programme.
All other probes have gone silent.

More worlds in this system await mapping.

— END OF LOG —

poi.universe.log.ending.1: We leave for the landing site at dawn. I'm leaving the terminal on. Maybe the next person can use it.
poi.universe.log.ending.2: If you're reading this, take whatever is in the crates. We won't need it anymore.
poi.universe.log.ending.3: End of entry. Power at four percent.
poi.universe.log.ending.4: I've left a copy of our navigation data on this terminal. Head toward the signal.
poi.universe.log.ending.5: More tomorrow. The aurora tonight is beautiful. We all went out to watch.
poi.universe.log.ending.6: (The rest of this entry is corrupted and cannot be read.)
poi.universe.log.event.1: Three Sentinels came this afternoon. They just watched the mining rig for a while, then left.
poi.universe.log.event.2: %1$s went out to check the pipeline and hasn't come back. The beacon shows the signal stopped in the eastern valley, not moving.
poi.universe.log.event.3: A meteor came down nearby and the shockwave shattered two windows. We saved the impact coordinates to the navigation data.
poi.universe.log.event.4: Someone went through the supply crates in storage, but the lock is untouched. %1$s says we must have miscounted.
poi.universe.log.event.5: The reactor readings have started to jump. We shut down half the equipment and keep a single light on at night.
poi.universe.log.event.6: The signal booster caught a repeating transmission, not on any of our frequencies. %1$s recorded it.
poi.universe.log.event.7: Another section of ground collapsed, opening a deep shaft. %1$s dropped a glowstick in. We never heard it land.
poi.universe.log.event.8: The company finally answered: outpost decommissioned, personnel to evacuate on their own. It didn't say how.
poi.universe.log.opening.1: Outpost %1$s, day %2$s of deployment. Log entry by %3$s.
poi.universe.log.opening.3: Automatic logging restored. Outpost %1$s, day %2$s, on duty: %3$s.
poi.universe.log.opening.4: Day %2$s. Outpost %1$s. This is %3$s. If anyone finds this recording—
poi.universe.log.situation.1: The supply ship is late again. %1$s locked the last crate of oxygen capsules away and says we ration from today.
poi.universe.log.situation.2: The drill rig died in last night's storm. %1$s worked on it all night and still couldn't get it turning.
poi.universe.log.situation.3: The ore here is richer than the survey promised. %1$s says one more season and we can all retire.
poi.universe.log.situation.4: %1$s insists there is knocking under the floor at night. I listened. Nothing.
poi.universe.log.situation.5: The comm array only picks up static. %1$s has realigned the antenna thirty times; the signal hasn't changed.
poi.universe.log.situation.6: The temperature swings get worse every day and our suit protection won't hold for long. %1$s has started coughing.
poi.universe.log.situation.7: We found a stone covered in symbols on the northern ridge. %1$s took pictures and says it can't be natural.
poi.universe.log.situation.8: Found a new creature today. %1$s gave it an awful name and logged it in the discovery log anyway.
poi.universe.lore.1.text: Traveler, you can hear us. Long ago we too set out from one small world, looked up at the sky, and believed the stars would never go dark.
poi.universe.lore.1.title: Echo
poi.universe.lore.10.text: At the heart of the cluster is something that swallows light. Our last fleet flew toward it. Some called it escape. Some called it going home.
poi.universe.lore.10.title: The Center
poi.universe.lore.11.text: You will build your rings and your shells too. We will not stop you; we cannot. We only want you to know what they cost.
poi.universe.lore.11.title: Choice
poi.universe.lore.12.text: If one day your sky begins to dim, remember to come back here and lay your hand on the stone. We will hear you.
poi.universe.lore.12.title: Last Words
poi.universe.lore.2.text: We learned to tame stars. The day the first ring closed around our sun, our nights were never dark again. We had more energy than we could ever use, so we went looking for more stars.
poi.universe.lore.2.title: The First Ring
poi.universe.lore.3.text: A thousand stars wrapped in our shells. Light flowed along the roads we laid, from one system to the next. We called it prosperity.
poi.universe.lore.3.title: The Web of Stars
poi.universe.lore.4.text: We hollowed out world after world. Forests became pits, oceans became coolant pools. Planets do not protest, so we heard nothing.
poi.universe.lore.4.title: Quiet Worlds
poi.universe.lore.5.text: Later we built the Sentinels to watch over the worlds that remained. They know no masters, only harm. The ones you meet today are their descendants.
poi.universe.lore.5.title: Sentinels
poi.universe.lore.6.text: We quarreled over the stars. Some wanted the shells torn down so starlight could reach the barren worlds again. Others said we still did not have nearly enough.
poi.universe.lore.6.title: Fracture
poi.universe.lore.7.text: The farthest systems began to dim, one after another. Not dying — being enclosed. Someone among us was building in secret, and we never learned who.
poi.universe.lore.7.title: Dimming
poi.universe.lore.8.text: Then came the Silence. Every channel went quiet at once, as if someone had closed a door. We never understood what lay on the other side.
poi.universe.lore.8.title: The Silence
poi.universe.lore.9.text: Those who remained raised these monoliths. We carved our memories into stone, because stone outlives us. Part of the survey data in your hands came from us.
poi.universe.lore.9.title: Monoliths
